items.title: How do Rust async runtimes (e.g. tokio) handle channels?
items.body:
I am a C programmer. I wrote a program which has a thread which does 2 things:

  • handlers network interface (receive requests and send responses);
  • waits for messages from other threads.

I used epoll in this thread. It handles network easily. However, in order to wait for messages, I have to use pipe to transfer message, just because the pipe's fd can be handled by epoll.

--

Now, I am learning Rust and its async part. I find that the async runtimes (e.g. tokio):

  • use epoll too;
  • can handle both network IO and channel;
  • However, I guess the channel should not be implemented by pipe.

So, my question is that, how do these runtimes handle channels (by epoll) as well as network IO? Or how do the channels wake up epoll when receiving messages?

In another words, where do the runtimes block at when there is no task to do? For example, in C program with epoll, it blocks at epoll_wait when no task.

I tried to read the code but there are too many encapsulation levels. It's hard to find the answer easy. So I come here.

items.title: How to use lazy_static with async/await initializer?
items.body:
I am using mongodb with tokio as my async runtime.

I want to initialize the MongoDB Client globally so I used the lazy-static crate. The problem is that the client connects asynchronously, and lazy_static! doesn't support the async keyword:

use mongodb::Client;

async {
    let client = Client::with_uri_str(&env_var("MONGO_URL")).await.unwrap();
}

So how can I initialize the client?

Related:

  • alternative to using 'await' with lazy_static! macro in rust?
  • Async/await support? on the lazy-static issue tracker

items.title: How to synchronise async runtimes
items.body:
We have a Python application that is implemented with the async runtime. Now we want to integrate a C library (with Cython) that runs its own event loop (e.g. epoll).

How can we integrate these two different runtime mechanisms. Is there a general pattern to synchronise these two codebases?

Eventually we might replace the Python code with Rust. So using a language-independent pattern would be nice.
